subject: Overlay VLAN stitching & late-binding overlay proposal — IaC review
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Alice Lim <alice.lim@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: EdgeOps Network <network@edgeops.io>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Overlay VLAN stitching & late-binding overlay proposal — IaC review

Hi all,

Following up from the architecture sync: we're proposing a late-binding overlay approach for the private deployment (VPC/on-prem) workstreams to support blue/green environment overlays without touching customer VLAN allocations. High level:

- Each customer gets a dedicated underlay VLAN space managed by their edge/SDN (RFC1918 ranges).
- Redwood will create ephemeral overlay networks (VXLAN/Geneve) stitched to the underlay via a small mapping table at provisioning time (late-binding).
- IaC footprint: Terraform for underlay attachments + CRDs, Helm charts for k8s overlay controllers, and Ansible for host-level interface config; CI validates idempotency and rollback.

Ask: Can the infra team review the proposed IaC artifacts for:
1) deterministic VLAN stitching rules (no async races during reconcilation)
2) safe defaults for overlapping RFC1918 ranges
3) CI tests to simulate partial failure during blue/green switch

I've attached a rough VLAN mapping (vlan-mapping.csv) and a short terraform subnet snippet. Please reply with blockers or mark changes inline in the Google diagram (link below).

Attachments: vlan-mapping.csv (csv), tf-subnet-snippet.tf (terraform)
Related: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcD_example_diagram

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Platform Engineer, Private Deploy
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Lim <alice.lim@acme-cloud.com>, EdgeOps Network <network@edgeops.io>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overlay VLAN stitching & late-binding overlay proposal — IaC review

+1 on the late-binding approach in principle. Couple of notes after a quick pass of the TF snippet:

- Overlap handling: we should encode a deterministic collision resolution policy in Terraform (e.g., prefer customer-provided allocation with the overlay picking the next free range) rather than implicit failures. I'll attach a tiny tf file (tf-subnet-snippet.tf) with a proposed locals block for allocation ordering.
- During reconciliation, the controller must be idempotent and tolerant to partial apply. Recommend: run a simulated drift step in CI (apply -> inject stale underlay -> apply) and assert that overlay attaches restore state.
- Security: ensure no accidental cross-tenant VXLAN leakage; need to validate VNI uniqueness and map to a tag in the k8s CRD.

I'll sketch the CI job later today; blockers for me now are clear contract around who owns the underlay cleanup (EdgeOps vs. customer) and a path for emergency rollback.

Attachment: tf-subnet-snippet.tf (terraform)

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Lim <alice.lim@acme-cloud.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeOps Network <network@edgeops.io>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 14:32:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Overlay VLAN stitching & late-binding overlay proposal — IaC review

Thanks Priya / Kimberly — good summary. A few constraints from our side (Acme Cloud) to avoid surprises when we stitch to customer-managed underlay: 

- We cannot guarantee contiguous VLAN blocks for every customer; some sites will have fragmented allocations. Your late-binding overlay needs a compacting algorithm (or fallback to multiple VNIs per customer site).
- Our carrier partners sometimes reassign VLAN IDs during maintenance windows; plan for a tagging reconciliation hook and non-destructive remap.
- We prefer VXLAN VNI assignment to be derived from a hash of (account-id, site-id) so collisions are extremely unlikely. We'll share a small PDF with regional constraints.

I've uploaded a diagram and a constraints PDF: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcD_example_diagram 
Attachment: acme-vlan-constraints.pdf (pdf)

We can run a staging test against one pilot site next week if you can provide the preview Helm values and a CI job to simulate VLAN reassign.

--
Alice Lim
Network Architect, Acme Cloud
alice.lim@acme-cloud.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Alice Lim <alice.lim@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: EdgeOps Network <network@edgeops.io>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overlay VLAN stitching & late-binding overlay proposal — IaC review

Nice feedback — thanks. Action items and next steps: 

1) Priya: add the allocation policy to the Terraform module (locals + plan-time validation), include a documented fallback when underlay fragments.
2) Kimberly: draft the CI matrix — steps: apply baseline, inject VLAN remap (simulated), reapply, assert overlay reconciliation; add idempotency checks and a canary switch for blue/green flip. Use GitLab pipeline template (below).
3) Alice / Acme: confirm whether the hash-based VNI derivation is acceptable for a pilot; if yes we'll implement as default and allow override in Helm values.

I've created a stub pipeline job in the infra repo and added INFRA-2347 to track the CI-ticket. Please review the pipeline template and add edge-case jobs.

Attachments: gitlab-pipeline-template.yml (yaml)
Related links: JIRA: INFRA-2347, https://gitlab.redwoodinc.com/infra/priv-deploy/-/blob/main/pipeline-templates/overlay-ci.yml

-Jordan
